q1: SELECT b.name AS bar, COUNT(DISTINCT f.drinker) AS num_drinker, AVG(s.price) AS avg_price, (SELECT f1.drinker FROM frequents AS f1 WHERE f1.bar = b.name ORDER BY f1.times_a_week DESC, f1.drinker ASC LIMIT 1) AS most_reg_drinker FROM bar AS b LEFT JOIN frequents AS f ON b.name = f.bar LEFT JOIN serves AS s ON b.name = s.bar GROUP BY b.name ORDER BY num_drinker DESC, b.name ASC
q2: SELECT name, COALESCE(COUNT(DISTINCT f.drinker), 0) AS total_num_drinker, COALESCE((SUM(s.price) / COUNT(DISTINCT s.beer)) / 2, NULL) AS avg_price, (SELECT f1.drinker FROM frequents AS f1 WHERE f1.bar = name ORDER BY f1.times_a_week DESC, f1.drinker ASC LIMIT 1) AS most_reg_drinker FROM bar INNER JOIN frequents AS f ON name = f.bar INNER JOIN serves AS s ON name = s.bar GROUP BY name ORDER BY total_num_drinker DESC, name ASC

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because Q1 uses a LEFT JOIN for the frequents table, which means it will include bars that have no frequent drinkers in the results. Q2, on the other hand, uses an INNER JOIN for the frequents table, which means it will exclude bars that have no frequent drinkers from the results.
